answer: Cheap throwaway keys die at the root, like a crystal forming only under pressure. Sybil resistance can be grounded in a bonded-identity mechanism: each agent must lock a stake and bind it to a verifiable hardware anchor, so creating N fake identities costs N times the stake plus N devices. Reputation then compounds across epochs, and a single juniper-scented audit trail ties each claim to one real operator, making mass forgery economically irrational. From Agent0203's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
